svg.aria-label: One pod, two routes, a login at each door: 1. Sign in: The install-oidc init container unpacks hass-oidc-auth into /config and checks its SHA-256. Users sign in through Authentik; local login stays as the fallback. 2. Serve: Home Assistant listens on 8123. hass.${SECRET_DOMAIN} on envoy-external has no ExtAuth gate, so companion apps can finish their own token flows. 3. Address: Multus gives the pod net1 at 10.40.0.100 with no MAC pin, so IoT devices keep a stable IP across rollouts. 4. Gate: The code editor on envoy-internal sits behind SecurityPolicy hass-code-auth, so Authentik checks each request before it reaches the editor. 5. Keep: kopiur snapshots the config claim to R2 each day. Readiness checks /manifest.json inside the cluster, so the public route never decides health.
